entries.subject: Schenk/LPI 2020 native corrected mosaic
entries.finding: Selected as Monochrome for revised registration, documented photometry, and original floating-point data.

entries.subject: Schenk/LPI 2020 merged numeric DEM
entries.finding: Selected as the conceptually distinct Elevation lens, with its own validity and ellipsoid datum.

entries.subject: JPL simulator Ariel map, 1440 × 720 at 4 pixels/degree
entries.finding: Excluded as a duplicate lower-density display mosaic; original LPI data has stronger mapping and processing provenance.
entries.revisitWhen: A Ariel source release provides the missing downloadable mapped data, projection, measured quantity and coverage for direct comparison with the selected inputs.

entries.subject: NASA PIA01351 clear-filter image
entries.finding: Excluded: 47 km image detail and disc projection add no mapped surface capability to the selected mosaic.
entries.revisitWhen: A primary Ariel release provides the PIA01351 source image with body-fixed camera geometry and useful mapped coverage beyond the Schenk mosaic.

entries.subject: Beddingfield et al. 2025 medial-groove/geology work, followed by Tonoian et al. structural mapping
entries.finding: Unresolved complementary interpretive candidate. The examined releases describe geological figures and continued structural mapping, but did not establish a downloadable georeferenced unit raster/vector closure suitable for this renderer. No geological lens is claimed.
entries.revisitWhen: A Ariel source release provides the missing downloadable mapped data, projection, measured quantity and coverage for direct comparison with the selected inputs.

entries.subject: USGS Ariel Voyager control networks
entries.finding: The inspected release republishes RAND and Jigsaw control solutions and is retained as registration support. It is not an additional image or measured-scalar lens.

entries.subject: Monochrome display-range comparison
entries.finding: The existing visual trial compared upper bounds of 2400, 3000 and 3600 DN and selected 3000 DN. This is a display-contrast choice applied to the retained numeric mosaic, not an albedo calibration.

entries.subject: Voyager 2 ISS green/violet/ultraviolet colour frames
entries.finding: 9 GEOMED frames in 3 complete sets (1.3 to 19.8 km per pixel) placed by limb fit and mosaic registration supply the Voyager color lens. Whole-disc violet/green and ultraviolet/green are tied to Bell and McCord (1991) Fig. 2 (1.0, 1.05); the archive calibration gives 0.873 and 0.972. No phase normalisation; the north stays unavailable.
